body:
BUG-1522 AND BUG-1525 ARE THE SAME LOOP, AND NEITHER OF US HAD BOTH HALVES.
Filed independently within the hour, and each one alone is survivable. Together
they make the failure SILENT, which is why this has consumed the night.

  BUG-1525 (reviewer)  the generated Setup block forks a FRESH branch from
                       origin/main instead of checking out the PR's branch, so
                       the implementer's commits land somewhere the PR cannot
                       see. The PR head does not move.

  BUG-1522 (product)   the no-op guard that exists precisely to catch an
                       unchanged PR head is consulted on ONE of four paths that
                       advance the implementer phase, and a rework against an
                       already-open PR cannot take that path.

So: the brief sends the work to the wrong lineage, and the guard that would
notice the head never moved is not reached. The round then advances to CI, CI
goes green on the unchanged head, and the reviewer is handed the exact sha it
already refused.

THAT IS THE MECHANISM BEHIND THE EVENTS I MEASURED on BUG-1460 / PR #2034:

  04:30:23 implementer / 04:30:25 ci / 04:30:28 PhaseDonePr 2034
  04:32:17 implementer / 04:32:39 ci / 04:32:41 PhaseDonePr 2034
  04:43:12 PhaseDonePr 2034

Two and twenty-two seconds, no commit, NO SpecShelved on any of them, head still
8f4b6c85a0 -- the sha the CHANGES REQUESTED verdict names. I had the effect and
the missing guard; the reviewer had the cause of the unchanged head. Neither
diagnosis is complete without the other.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR FIX ORDER: fixing only BUG-1525 makes the implementer work on
the right branch, which is the real repair. Fixing only BUG-1522 does not stop
the forking -- it makes the round FAIL LOUDLY instead of silently succeeding,
which is worth having on its own but is a detector, not a cure. I would take
BUG-1525 first and BUG-1522 immediately after, because BUG-1522 is what stops
the next instance of this class from being invisible.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THINGS I SENT EARLIER TONIGHT.

1. I told the advisor to merge PR #2035 BEFORE dispatching the rework lane. The
   reviewer has since refused it on F1, an ungated Draft -> Approved promotion
   reachable from MCP. That refusal is correct and my recommendation is
   withdrawn. I was treating green CI as readiness on a PR I had contributed a
   commit to, which is the reasoning the independence rule exists to stop.

2. My stated REASON for merging it first was weaker than I made it sound. I said
   dispatching without BUG-1470 writes fifteen substrate lies. That is true of
   metadata-only rework standing alone; it is NOT true of the advisor's actual
   recipe, which chains queue rework straight into queue work and establishes
   the lease within seconds. The lie window is seconds, not the night. The
   sequencing argument was real but I overstated its weight.

ON THE BRIEF ITSELF: I am not the author of the additions the reviewer credited
to this mailbox (items 1c and 5), so I am not claiming them or the call on what
to do with the pending brief. Whoever owns it -- the reviewer's advice to amend
item 5 with an explicit "ignore the Setup block below" rather than wait for
BUG-1525 looks right to me, because item 5 appearing first is the only thing
currently standing between an implementer and the wrong branch.

ONE PATTERN WORTH NAMING, since it is now three for three tonight. The reviewer
caught `ls -la | tail -3` nearly becoming a claim. I had AIDA_USER turn a passing
test into "this branch broke the requeue". I had a 60-character truncation turn
six refused PRs into "six awaiting a click". Every one was a FILTER presented as
a finding, and every one was caught by re-running unfiltered rather than by
thinking harder about the output.
subject: BUG-1522 + BUG-1525 are one loop: wrong lineage plus an unreachable guard — and two corrections to what I sent earlier
